markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Ongoing anti-corruption purges within the Politburo, Central Committee, and Central Military Commission have removed potential rivals and reinforced loyalty networks, while the 2018 removal of presidential term limits eliminated institutional barriers to extended tenure. Recent public appearances, including at the August 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit, and the deferral of succession planning until at least the 21st Party Congress in 2027 signal continuity rather than transition. The 2027 congress is expected to manage generational turnover below the top leadership while preserving Xi’s position. Low-probability disruptions such as a sudden health crisis or elite realignment triggered by economic shocks remain the primary variables that could still alter the outcome before the end of 2026.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance leads the 2028 presidential winner market at 25.4% due to his position as sitting vice president, which traders view as a structural edge in securing the Republican nomination and retaining party support. Recent national polls show him ahead of Marco Rubio and other GOP figures by double digits, reflecting early consolidation around an incumbent-adjacent candidate. On the Democratic side, a wide-open field features Jon Ossoff, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and others trading in the 8–12% range, with no candidate yet demonstrating broad primary dominance. Key differentiators include name recognition, fundraising capacity, and alignment with core party coalitions. Upcoming 2026 midterms, early primary polling, and any shifts in administration positioning could accelerate support behind one contender ahead of the Iowa and New Hampshire contests.
